## Purpose
Top-level view for the IDE-initiated "handoff" pipeline (`/flowin-handoff`): fetches a handoff session by token, drives its live pipeline over a dedicated WebSocket, and renders the agent panel + diff/tests/compliance preview panels, including PAT onboarding and expiry states.

## Shape
- `HandoffWorkflow` — the main export; gates on auth, fetches the session via `getHandoff`, hydrates completed/failed state from persisted `pipeline_output` (coding summary, edit results, PR info, test/compliance reports) by replaying them through the same `handleMessage` reducer a live run uses, and opens `useHandoffSocket` only while the session is actively running.
- `useHandoffPipelineState` — external hook supplying the `state`/`handleMessage`/`setPipelineStatus` reducer that both the hydration path and the live WS path feed into.
- `wsBridge` — adapts the app-wide `StreamMessage` shape to the narrower `HandoffStreamMessage` shape the handoff reducer expects.
- Renders `HandoffAgentPanel` (left) and `HandoffPreviewPanel` (right) once past onboarding/expiry gating; `IntegrationsCard` is shown instead when the user has no GitHub PAT saved yet.

## Why this shape
The component intentionally mirrors the existing pptx/user-stories workflow layout (per its own docstring) so a handoff run "looks the same" as other pipelines to the user, and it deliberately hydrates historical/completed sessions through the identical event-reducer a live run uses rather than a separate rendering path, so the Diff/Tests/Compliance tabs behave the same whether the data arrived live or on page reload.
